page: Amazon Web Services c5ad.large is a compute-optimized instance powered by an AMD EPYC 7R32 processor running at 3.3 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. It features 2 vCPUs (1 physical core with 2 threads) and 4.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz. The instance is built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor and includes 75 GB of local NVMe SSD instance storage, alongside a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate a performance profile suited for specific single-threaded tasks but limited in multi-core scaling. The instance achieves average performance in single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression, as well as an average Geekbench single-core score. However, multi-core CPU performance, memory bandwidth, and database operations fall into the lower percentiles, with stress-ng and Passmark CPU scores ranking in the bottom 10%.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c5ad.large offers a low-cost entry point into compute-optimized hardware with dedicated CPU allocation and high-speed local NVMe storage. The primary tradeoff is the low memory capacity of 4.0 GB and constrained multi-core performance. This instance is best suited for lightweight compute tasks, single-threaded batch processing, basic web serving, and development workloads that benefit from fast local temporary storage but do not require high memory or parallel processing power.
